newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent recovers losses, closes just 2 cts off.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent recovers losses, closes just 2 cts off.

text.p: IPE Brent futures retraced most of the ground lost on Thursday after speculators in New York sold the expiring August gasoline contract and finished just 2 cents down on the day at $18.95 a barrel.

September Brent's late surge upwards from an intra-day low of $18.45 came after the effect of the speculative dump of gasoline futures wore off and tight physical crude fundamentals and worries over delayed Iraqi exports reasserted themselves.
The climb left front-month Brent close to the $19 mark it has been trying to break through convincingly since Wednesday's gasoline-driven 38 cent climb.
"It was very, very choppy today," said one broker
Brent's strength has derived from the U.S. gasoline market, where industry data suggest heavy use has eaten into stocks and plant problems at refineries have limited supplies.
August gasoline eventually expired more than three cents down after speculators cut their losses, but fundamental strength seemed to transfer to the September contract, which ended four cents up.
News of a refinery fire in Venezuala that will cut at least 60,000 barrels per day of product output helped bolster the U.S market and gave European market bulls a lift.
A lack of clear news on when Iraq will resume crude exports was also cited as helping values higher.
U.N. sources indicate that this weekend they could conclude the aid distribution plan Baghdad insists must be finalised before it will resume crude shipments suspended since late May.
But brokers say the news was not definite enough to push values down for long. "The less clear news there is on Iraq the more bullish it is for us," said one IPE floor trader.
Earlier gas oil settled $1.75 down on the day at $167.75 a tonne, and should rise on Friday's open to catch up with Brent crude's late gains.

Dealers said the market was still vulnerable to the Iraq effect, given Baghdad should resume exports at much higher volumes than before. If a definite start date emerged it would start a heavy sell-off
Brent's failure to push through the $19 mark also raised worries over how long it could hold near that eight-week high.

"If it had closed above $19 that would have been technically supportive," said one. "But finishing below $19 is bad, especially with the expiry of a product contract that has been one of the main strengths of the market."
